protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 2 of 3; refute not confirm; verify C2-D046-01 and ADV-D046-T1-01 landed
summary: Both turn-1 findings landed and the new clause 4 survives testing claim by claim. C2-D046-01 is repaired in the D-044 form, naming the restore target explicitly. Clause 4, which is entirely new substance from the other reviewer's finding, makes five checkable assertions and every one holds: file 09's Review refresh rule really does require regenerating the baseline, resolving every row, and recording the five-lane disposition -- exactly the three limbs clause 4 says a later substantive change still triggers -- and v1-authority-baseline.json /sources/1 really is {path: docs/coop/IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md, sha256: e809d439…} with no §6 segment, which I read at the bytes rather than accepting. That retained whole-file snapshot is consistent with adopted D-044's 'Those files stay whole-document until a later MEASURED regeneration'. I re-ran the §6 segment hash rather than trusting an unchanged extraction block, re-verified the empty-set claim the new alternative now asserts, and confirmed clauses 1 through 3 are byte-identical after my first extraction attempt produced a boundary artifact I chased down rather than reported.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 6d5221923fad418c7faba49a0fac4d9bab12880cb793a0dd1b5887df978f67ed both times, matching the dispatch's expected digest. No drift.

C2-D046-01 landed and in the precedent form I asked for. Reversibility now reads 'Compound after the rewrite lands. Overturn: C-D046, plus restore of the prior whole-file freeze pin e809d439… as the Key sealed laws source pin.' That supplies the restore limb a compound overturn needs, names the restore target and its value, and matches adopted D-044's 'Overturn: C-D044, plus restore of the prior scope clause.'

The attack 'unreproducible §6 hash' fails, and I re-derived it this turn rather than relying on turn 1 or on the extraction block being unchanged. sed lines 1405-1580 of the live freeze hashes to bfa71f42fb1e25d7d9556ea7549723b8e91af205147d3cca0d34558e1eba3b5e, the cited value.

ADV-D046-T1-01 landed as clause 4, and I tested each of its assertions instead of accepting a finding I did not raise. Assertion one, that file 09 has a 'Refreshing this matrix' rule: it does, at the 'Review refresh rule' heading, reading 'Refreshing this matrix requires regenerating the baseline, resolving every row, and recording the five-lane review disposition in the central register. A hash match alone is insufficient: a pin is not a selector reader, a pass is not an application, and an application is not a freeze disposition.'

Assertion two, that clause 4's 'full baseline / every-row / five-lane refresh' names that rule's obligations: it maps limb for limb onto 'regenerating the baseline, resolving every row, and recording the five-lane review disposition'. The compression is accurate, not a paraphrase that drops one.

Assertion three, that the classification is sound: the rule's trigger is a refresh of the matrix, and its own gloss is about not over-reading evidence -- a pin is not a selector reader, a pass is not an application -- rather than about pin maintenance. This act re-pins one row's source citation at finer granularity over the same file, the same section and the same laws, and re-resolves nothing. Treating it as outside the refresh rule is defensible on the rule's own text.

Assertion four, that 'the source path, freeze bytes, section selector, laws 1–19, standings, and every other row remain unchanged': the path stays docs/coop/IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md by clause 1; the freeze bytes are unchanged and the segment is a subset of them; the section is the same §6 the row already cited as 'laws 1–19 in full'; I confirmed at turn 1 that laws 1 through 19 all fall inside 1405-1580; and clause 2 leaves every other row alone.

Assertion five, the baseline claim, which is the one I could not confirm from anything seen earlier. v1-authority-baseline.json has a 49-entry sources list and /sources/1 is exactly {"path": "docs/coop/IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md", "sha256": "e809d4395f394a507c36c23c069d566c838b2283c931b6d2d13797be53406dbd"} -- the whole-file freeze snapshot, containing no §6 segment. The JSON-pointer path clause 4 cites resolves to what it says it resolves to.

The deliberate asymmetry clause 4 creates is consistent with the adopted record rather than novel: after this act file 09's row pins §6 while the baseline keeps the whole-file snapshot, and adopted D-044 states 'Those files stay whole-document until a later MEASURED regeneration' -- one occurrence, matched over normalized whitespace. Retaining the snapshot is the position already adopted, not a new exception minted here.

The attack 'waives future substantive refresh' fails. Clause 4 closes 'Any later substantive matrix change still triggers the full baseline / every-row / five-lane refresh', and no other sentence in the draft relaxes it. The attack 'treats this as a full matrix refresh' fails from the other side: the new alternative 'Defer and perform the full matrix refresh' is rejected because 'this conversion does not change a cited property of any row', which is true -- the property is laws 1-19 before and after, and only the pin's granularity moves.

The new alternative now asserts my own turn-1 measurement, and I re-verified it rather than letting my earlier count stand: 'The set of other whole-document freeze standing pins in file 09 is empty' holds, with the freeze whole-file digest occurring exactly once in file 09 and the blueprint digest zero times.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on all six: file 09 b96f6236…, freeze e809d439…, freeze §6 bfa71f42…, file 08 80fc55d1…, COORD 731d8613…, plus my turn-1 verdict at ca47bf5c… and the Codex turn-1 verdict at 6185cc99…. Each measured by me against live bytes.

My turn-1 verdict is characterized exactly as 'OBJECT, 1 SHOULD-FIX', which is what I returned -- verdict OBJECT, mustFix 0, shouldFix 1, single id C2-D046-01. The disposition table records it as ACCEPTED with an accurate description of what changed.

I verified the prompt's byte-identity claim rather than accepting it, and pursued my own first result rather than reporting it. My initial extraction of clauses 1 through 3 hashed differently between drafts, which would have been a finding; the cause was my range boundary, not the drafts, since turn 2's clause 4 sits between clause 3 and the Alternatives heading and shifted what my sed range captured. Extracting precisely -- from '1. Convert the Key sealed laws' through the '(MF-6).' line -- gives 11 lines and 95155239c538d8f051ae4c430ecf8375 in both, and diff reports them identical.
The token-loss diff over the whole draft returns NOTHING lost, so this repair is purely additive and the silent-drop failure mode does not recur.

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED or condition-1 discharge' and 'file 08 or baseline edited' both fail. SATISFIED occurs twice, both refusals; clause 3 states 'Condition 1 does not discharge. Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization'; clause 2 declines file 08 and the baseline JSON; and git reports file 08, file 09, the freeze, both baseline JSONs and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md all unmodified, so nothing has been pre-applied ahead of adoption.

The MF-6 framing remains right for this act: 'File-09 content change is this D-000-reviewed act (MF-6)' — this entry IS the MF-6 act for file 09 rather than deferring to one, which is the correct inversion of D-044's 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6)'.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex turn-2 review of D-046. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

The Codex turn-1 verdict, hashed but never opened. I know ADV-D046-T1-01 only through this entry's disposition table and the dispatch, and I verified the substance of the clause it produced rather than Codex's statement of the finding. The entry characterizes that verdict as 'OBJECTIONS, 1 SHOULD-FIX'; I verified the digest 6185cc99… and not the class or count.
Whether NOTE-D046-T1-01, carried as an adoption instruction that is 'not a merits condition', is correctly so classified. It is Codex's note and I have not read it.

Whether the §6 segment's content is correct as law. I verified the boundaries, the hash, and that laws 1 through 19 are inside; not that any law says what the claim matrix relies on it to say. That is the row owner's question.

Whether the Key sealed laws row's prose survives the conversion unchanged. File 09 is not edited this cycle, so there is nothing yet to compare; that check belongs to the commit this entry authorizes.

Whether the baseline's other 48 sources include whole-document pins that a later MEASURED regeneration should convert. I read /sources/1 because clause 4 names it; I did not audit the remaining entries, and D-044 has already placed the baseline outside conversion until that regeneration.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero findings and I state what I attacked, because most of this turn's new substance is a clause produced by the other reviewer's finding rather than mine, and that is exactly the material I have no stake in and must therefore test hardest. Clause 4 makes five assertions and I checked all five against bytes I read myself: the refresh rule exists and says what clause 4 says it says; the three-limb compression is faithful; the classification is defensible on the rule's own text; the unchanged-elements list holds; and /sources/1 is the whole-file snapshot at the exact JSON pointer cited. I also re-derived the §6 hash rather than assuming an unchanged extraction block stays correct, and when my own first byte-identity check disagreed with the prompt I chased the discrepancy to my range boundary instead of filing it.
